afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 210827
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
123 AM MST Sat Nov 21 2026


.KEY MESSAGES...

- The overall pattern will favor dry and tranquil conditions
  across the Desert Southwest through at least the Thanksgiving 
  Weekend. 
  
- Temperatures over the next several days will average a few 
  degrees below normal before a warming trend pushes readings to 
  above seasonal levels by the back half of next week. 

  
&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Current objective analysis reveals a dynamic pattern across the 
western CONUS as numerous weather regimes encompass the region. A 
positively tilted trough at the southern extent of this complex 
setup will advance through Arizona this morning, but will not 
result in any appreciable changes in conditions. As this feature 
moves through, heights aloft will continue their multi-day 
downward trend, albeit at a much faster rate than the previous few
days, which will allow for a bit of day-to-day cooling across our
forecast area. Highs for the lower deserts this afternoon are 
only expected to top out in the middle 60s to low 70s, around 5 
degrees or so below normal for this time of year. The forecasted 
high for Phoenix currently stands at 69 degrees, and if that were 
to be realized, it would be the first time since February 20th 
that a sub-70 high temperatures is seen at the station. It is not
out of the realm of possibility that virga or very light shower 
activity is seen over far southeastern Gila County this morning 
given sufficient enough lift and mid-level moisture, but precip 
chances are only around 20% and any accumulations are likely to be
minimal at best. Better chances exist further east over the more 
orographically enhanced terrain of the White Mountains. 

The above-mentioned shortwave will not stick around for long as 
model guidance has it migrating over the Great Plains by Saturday 
evening. This will allow for atmospheric temperatures to recover a 
bit, but broad troughing will continue across the western CONUS 
through at least the start of the workweek, keeping any noticeable 
warming trends at bay for now. Though afternoon highs will recover 
slightly on Sunday, mainly for south-central Arizona, readings in 
the upper 60s to lower 70s will be common for lower elevation 
locations through Monday. 

&&

.LONG TERM /TUESDAY THROUGH NEXT SATURDAY/...  
Not much in the way of change can be expected for the longer term 
outlook as the broader flow pattern promotes a continuation of 
benign conditions. Model guidance points towards a slight rise in 
heights aloft as we progress through the middle portion of the week, 
likely initiating a gradual warming trend for the region during this 
timeframe. A greater upward trend in atmospheric heights is shown 
taking place by Thanksgiving as an unseasonably strong area of high 
pressure sets up west of the Baja Peninsula. The good news is, the 
position of this ridge will put the Desert Southwest under the 
influence of cooler northwesterly flow, which will likely prevent
temperatures that are completely out of the ordinary for the end 
of November. Even though above-normal readings will make a return 
as early as Wednesday, daily highs during the back half of the 
week should remain quite pleasant with lower desert readings in 
the middle to upper 70s, with perhaps a few spots reaching the 
lower 80s by next weekend. With that being said however, it would 
not be surprising to see forecasted highs for Thursday and onward
trend higher from their current position as the NBM tends to be 
on the cooler side 6-10 days out.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0037Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
No major aviation concerns are expected through the TAF period.
FEW low clouds will continue to move east, with FEW-SCT high
clouds filtering into the region tomorrow evening. Westerly
evening winds will remain westerly overnight, and are not 
expected to do their typical E shift. Winds will be light aob 7 kt
and may become variable at times. The winds will reestablish 
their typical diurnal pattern by tomorrow evening.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
No major aviation concerns are expected during the next 24 hours.
Skies will remain mostly clear through most of the TAF period,
with SCT-BKN high cirrus clouds moving in by mid-afternoon
tomorrow. At KIPL, winds will remain out of the W/NW, with winds
speeds dropping to 7 kt or less over the next few hours. At KBLH,
winds will remain their typical N/NW direction overnight, with 
speeds aob 8 kt.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER... 
Dry and tranquil conditions will be common across the region
through the next several days. Outside of a slight spike on
Monday, MinRHs values will hover between 15-30% through most of
the forecast period, while cool overnight lows will result in
decent to good overnight recovery. Winds overall are expected to
be light and favor diurnal trends. Temperatures will hover near to
slightly below normal levels through the front half of the
upcoming week ahead of a warming later in the forecast period. 

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
Gila: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area due to water releases from the dam. 
Water releases remain around 3000 cfs. This will have the 
potential to flood farm fields and low water crossings along the 
river downstream from the dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Freeze Warning until 9 AM MST this morning for AZZ563.

     Freeze Warning from midnight tonight to 9 AM MST Sunday for 
     AZZ563.

CA...Freeze Warning until 8 AM PST Saturday for CAZ560.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...RW
LONG TERM...RW
AVIATION...Gibbons 
FIRE WEATHER...RW
HYDROLOGY...Lojero/Benedict
